claims: n-179-candidate.yaml is a packing.squares:Witness/v2 file (corners, rational scalars, 179 squares) whose exact rational side, rounded up at 12 places, #959 prints as the bound, 13.880960371559. Its exact coordinates were produced by this repository's packing-witness promote --strategy robust-rational at c8448724 from the lab's decimal pose, n-179-decimal-pose.yaml, with center_dilation '1' and no dilation: pairs separated by at least about 2e-13, the squares that set the left wall, the bottom wall and the side touching them exactly, and other squares near a wall clearing it by up to about 1e-12. An upper bound only: no KKT, local-optimality, rigidity or global-optimality claim. The issue says it improves and supersedes the author's own #954 (13.881367160110, T-291) by 4.068e-4, from the same method on a later batch, and that #954 stays a verified bound.

n179-witness.json is the same file as JSON. packing-witness-verify.txt is the author's run of this repository's packing-witness verify at c8448724 on the witness placed under packing/witnesses/known-best/ (VERIFIED, exact-algebraic, 15931 pairs); sqcheck-output.txt is the author's run of verifier/sqcheck.py, an exact checker the source says was written separately from this repository's code (VALID, exact rational, the exact side rounded up at 15 places). The issue says sqcheck.py also certified the decimal pose in interval arithmetic before promotion. Those statements are the author's; no source program ran here.

The issue and README say the packing was found by an AI-run band-design search, new for #954's filing: tilted squares from a registry packing of the same family laid along the diagonal as a seed band; simulated annealing in a reduced model in which the tilted squares move freely and the axis-parallel squares sit on the two wall-anchored staircase lattices, present or absent, with the overlap of the squares that must be kept as energy; then one quench with Evan Daniel's ALM+SLP code from evand/square-packing search/packer at bb4cc78e, MIT. The band is built from the tilted squares of the registry's n = 70 packing (Ryan Xu, found_by; improved by Evan Daniel and PingYou Ltd; side 8.880960371555579595), as in #954: a two-row band of 20 squares at -40.7505 degrees along the diagonal, the band where x + y <= 16 plus a second copy shifted by (5, 5) where x + y > 16, 35 tilted squares. It came from a later batch of the same scan as a mutation of such a seed (band parameter 4.4245 where #954's seed has 4.2495), annealed at side 13.88105 (3e6 moves, energy 0.0035), then quenched to 13.880960371558; two further jobs of the batch reach the same side to 1.5e-13 from the same band and from a different one (179ha/207a, shifted by (-1, -1)). They say its side is 2.64e-12 above side(70) + 5 = 13.880960371555579595 and that they have not shown the packing is that construction. They report, against the registry packing matched by assignment up to the square's symmetries: 143 of 179 centres move by more than 1e-3, 48 by more than 0.05 (largest 0.889); 43 squares re-tilted by more than 1 degree (largest 44.36); 36 squares tilted by more than 0.5 degree against the record's 35. They ask that the improvement be credited to Doğa Özden, the band's source packing (n = 70) and the current record to their holders as the registry lists them, and the local optimizer to Evan Daniel. The issue says the search and its code were written and run by AI agents and that the checks were run by code that did not produce the packing; the issue and repository were prepared and posted by Özden's AI agent, which uses the account kenaznia-doga; Özden directed the work.

The issue states first that the Kaggle per-puzzle leaderboard lists a side-only entry at 179, 13.880960371556 (team Nevska, 2026-11-07), unpublished and stating no packing, and that this side is 2.2e-12 above it (3e-12 for the 12-place claim) and does not beat it. The best public Kaggle per-puzzle packing it found at 179, 13.883795490524 (kirilltym), is above this side.
